problem: The sentence defining x(t) is corrupted: "x(t)=0 for t−2t for t≥0" is unreadable, so the student cannot see the signal being transformed.
fix: step 1: x(t)=0 for t<0 and x(t)=e−2t for t≥0. The energy is finite: E=∫0∞e−4tdt=1/4=0.25.

problem: The text "For τx(−τ)=Rx(τ) for real x" is broken and loses the whole argument for negative lag; as printed it tells the student nothing about how Rx is found for τ<0.
fix: step 4: For τ<0, put τ=−σ with σ>0. By direct computation Rx(−σ)=e−2σ/4, and for a real x, Rx(−τ)=Rx(τ). Hence Rx(τ)=e−2|τ|/4 for all τ.

problem: Saying flatly that the time-average autocorrelation of a power signal has a Fourier transform hides that this is a generalized transform: for a periodic signal Rx(τ) is periodic and Sx(ω) is a train of impulses, not an ordinary function.
fix: For a power signal the (generalized) Fourier transform of the time-average autocorrelation is the power spectral density Sx(ω): Rx(τ) ↔ Sx(ω), and P=(1/2π)∫Sx(ω)dω. For a periodic signal this transform is a sum of impulses at the harmonic frequencies.
